### Observed differences

- The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A22 and A14 roughly halved: in the earlier window these gaps averaged about 0.93 hours (median about 0.95 hours), while in the later window they averaged about 0.44 hours (median about 0.45 hours) — a shift of roughly half an hour, seen across 43 gaps before and 40 after; a difference this large appeared in about 1 of 2,000 random re-splits [TWAIT002].
- The same shortening appears between A17 and A14: the average gap fell from about 0.19 hours to about 0.08 hours (median about 0.14 to about 0.07 hours), based on 18 gaps before and 32 after, again with about 1 in 2,000 re-splits reaching this difference [TWAIT001].
- Both qualifying items come from the time family, which produced 2 items where an unchanged process would produce about 0.01; the control-flow family produced no items against 0.3 expected, so no structural difference passed the thresholds [TWAIT001, TWAIT002].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a timing change centred on A14: in the later window, the elapsed time between consecutive completion events leading into A14 is about half of what it was in the earlier window, both from A22 (about 0.93 to 0.44 hours on average) and from A17 (about 0.19 to 0.08 hours). The support is direct, since TWAIT measures exactly these elapsed gaps, and consistent, since both items point the same way while the time family yielded 2 items against roughly 0.01 expected by chance; the complete absence of control-flow items fits a pure timing change, which needs no structural counterpart [TWAIT001, TWAIT002].

Limitations: both items share A14, so they may reflect a single underlying difference rather than two independent ones, and the A17–A14 item rests on modest counts (18 and 32 gaps). TWAIT also cannot show where the shortening resides — in A14's own completion, in the predecessors, or in fewer or faster steps between the pair — and the evidence cannot rule out such an adjacency or placement explanation [TWAIT001, TWAIT002].

Other differences: none beyond the two timing items above [TWAIT001, TWAIT002].
